1.title: Encryption, Certificates and Secrets
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Encryption, Certificates and Secrets. It covers the exam area Domain two: Security. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Apply encryption at rest and in transit (two point two.one). Manage certificates with A C M and Private C A (two point two.two). Select client-side or server-side encryption (two point two.three). Use encryption keys to encrypt and decrypt data (two point two.four). Generate certificates and S S H keys for development (two point two.five). Identify, mask and limit access to sensitive data (two point two.six). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain two: Security (twenty-six percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: Encryption at rest and in transit
1.text: Encryption at rest and in transit. At rest. Data stored on disk or in a service is encrypted (S three, E B S, Dynamo D B, R D S and others support it, mostly with A W S K M S). In transit. Data moving over a network uses T L S (H T T P S).

1.title: AWS KMS
1.text: A W S K M S. A W S Key Management Service creates and controls encryption keys. K M S key (formerly C M K). The key resource; the key material never leaves K M S unencrypted. A W S owned or A W S managed or customer managed keys. Owned: invisible; managed: created by A W S in your account for a service; customer managed: you control the policy, rotation and deletion. Key policy. The resource policy that controls who can use or manage the key (I A M alone is not enough without it).

1.title: AWS KMS, continued
1.text: A W S K M S. Envelope encryption. Use a data key to encrypt large data; encrypt the data key with the K M S key. Encrypt or Decrypt. Direct operations on data up to four K B. Generate Data Key. Returns a plaintext data key and the same key encrypted; use the plaintext, then discard it and store the encrypted copy.

1.title: AWS KMS, continued
1.text: A W S K M S. The figure shows this: Envelope encryption: a data key encrypts the data, the K M S key encrypts the data key. Exam tip: Data larger than four K B equals envelope encryption with Generate Data Key. Control over key rotation and policy equals customer managed key.

1.title: Server-side or client-side
1.text: Server-side or client-side. S S E-S three. Who encrypts: S three with S three-managed keys. When to choose: Simplest at-rest encryption. S S E-K M S. Who encrypts: S three with a K M S key. When to choose: Need audit (Cloud Trail) and key control. S S E-C. Who encrypts: S three with a key you supply on each request. When to choose: You hold the keys. Client-side. Who encrypts: Your code before upload (for example, the A W S Encryption S D K). When to choose: Data must be encrypted before it leaves the client.

1.title: Certificates and SSH keys
1.text: Certificates and S S H keys. A W S Certificate Manager (A C M). Provision, manage and renew public T L S certificates for E L B, Cloud Front, A P I Gateway; free for public certificates. A W S Private C A. Issue private certificates for internal services and devices. E C two key pairs or S S H keys. Sign in to instances; generate for development; protect the private key.

1.title: Sensitive data and secrets
1.text: Sensitive data and secrets. Store secrets (passwords, A P I keys). A W S Secrets Manager: automatic rotation (through Lambda), fine-grained access, encrypted with K M S, cross-Region replication; billed per secret. Store configuration and simple secrets. Systems Manager Parameter Store: String, String List, Secure String (K M S); standard tier has no charge; no built-in rotation. Find and mask personal data (P I I, P H I). Amazon Macie finds sensitive data in S three; Cloud Watch Logs data protection masks it; Bedrock Guardrails filters it in A I traffic; limit access with I A M, resource policies and K M S key policies. Exam tip: "Rotate database credentials automatically" equals Secrets Manager. "Cheap configuration values and a few secrets" equals Parameter Store. Never hard-code secrets or put them in environment variables in plain text.

1.title: Sensitive data and secrets, continued
1.text: Sensitive data and secrets. Exam tip: S S E-K M S gives key control and Cloud Trail audit; S S E-S three is the simplest; S S E-C means you send the key each time.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An application must encrypt a five megabytes file with a K M S key. What is the right approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Use envelope encryption with Generate Data Key. Direct Encrypt is limited to four K B, so use a data key.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team needs audit logs of every use of the encryption key for S three objects. Which option fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: S S E-K M S. K M S usage is logged in Cloud Trail.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Database credentials must rotate automatically every thirty days. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A W S Secrets Manager. Secrets Manager offers built-in rotation.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A public website behind Cloud Front needs a free managed T L S certificate that renews automatically. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A W S Certificate Manager. A C M provisions and renews public certificates.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Data must be encrypted before it leaves the client application. Which option fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Client-side encryption. Client-side encryption protects data before upload.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A Lambda function reads an A P I key. What is the most secure approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Retrieve it from Secrets Manager at runtime with a role. Fetch secrets securely with a role instead of hard-coding.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the largest payload kms:Encrypt accepts directly? Answer: four K B. Question two. What does Generate Data Key return? Answer: A plaintext data key and the same key encrypted under the K M S key. Question three. Which key type gives you control of rotation and policy? Answer: A customer managed key.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which service issues private certificates for internal use? Answer: A W S Private C A. Question five. Which service has built-in secret rotation? Answer: Secrets Manager. Question six. What does S S E-C mean? Answer: S three encrypts using a key you supply with each request.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. K M S: key policy, envelope encryption, four K B direct limit, customer managed keys. S three options: S S E-S three, S S E-K M S (audit), S S E-C, client-side. Certificates: A C M (public, renews), Private C A (internal). Secrets: Secrets Manager (rotation) versus Parameter Store (cheap, Secure String).
